newsitem.title: THAILAND: Sluggish commodities prices hit Thai exports.
newsitem.headline: Sluggish commodities prices hit Thai exports.

text.p: Poor world prices led to sluggish commodities exports from Thailand in February, a senior Bank of Thailand official said.

Kleothong Hetrakul, chief economist at the central bank, attributed the sharp drop in exports for the month to bearish global commodities prices, especially for tapioca and rubber which were Thailand's key agricultural exports.

The country's exports in February contracted 5.5 percent to 108.6 billion baht (US$415.4 million). Commodities exports fetched only 11.5 billion baht, a hefty 24.5 percent drop from the same period last year.
"The value of commodities exports dropped in line with the sliding world prices," she said.

Kloethong said although rice prices were more bullish, export values were lower as the quantity exported had dropped. The value of rice exports during January-February dropped by 25 percent while the amount dropped 33 percent. The value of rubber exports dropped 16 percent and tapioca 25 percent during the same period, she said.
Thailand aims to export 5.5 million tonnes of rice, 1.69 million tonnes of rubber and more than 4.0 million tonnes of tapioca.
Kleothong said rice exports are expected to pick up in the second half of the year on the back of robust demand.
"In February, players in the market took a wait and see stance as the second crop was due to come into the market soon. They looked at the price trend before deciding to sell or buy," she said.
"I don't think the drop in rice exports indicates that we are losing our competitive edge to other rice exporting countries. We still can sell high grade rice very well," she added.
Traders said the high Thai rice prices alienated lower tier buyers who increasingly turned to Vietnam or Pakistan for cheaper rice.
